title: Request Fabric: Edge Observability Proxy for Hybrid SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: SDKs instrumented across multiple languages and several proxy or edge hops produce inconsistent trace contexts, duplicated spans, and variable sampling decisions. Our client libraries and edge components each implement slightly different propagation heuristics which complicates debugging latency and error spikes. Instrumentation can also add noticeable overhead near ingress points where we need strict SLOs.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'Request Fabric' observability proxy that sits at the edge (or run as a sidecar for Dedicated/Private installs) to: normalize incoming trace context, apply centralized sampling and prioritization policies, enrich request context with routing and tenant metadata, defer heavy span processing to background workers, and provide a single hook for SDKs (and uninstrumented clients) to opt into Redwood's tracing conventions. This should reduce tracing noise, make sampling deterministic for downstream services, and keep p50/p95 ingress latency overhead <1ms where possible.

Scope: 
- A small proxy binary (Go) with pluggable propagation normalizers (W3C traceparent, B3, legacy custom headers).
- Configurable sampling rules keyed by route, tenant, and token/plan.
- Lightweight synchronous annotations for latency-sensitive paths; full span creation is offloaded to an async processor via an internal queue.
- SDK-facing middleware bindings: a shim layer that maps SDK start/end hooks to the proxy's light annotation API so SDKs can remain minimally invasive.
- Observability outputs: telemetry metrics (ingress latency, sampling rate, queue depth, dropped spans), logs (structured JSON), and trace events forwarded to the main tracing pipeline.

Non-goals: replacing the full SDK tracing stack, implementing advanced span enrichment in the proxy, or changing cross-service sampling downstream of services that have their own sampling policies.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy binary builds and runs in staging; config loaded from S3/k8s ConfigMap
Trace context normalized across at least 3 propagation formats when passing through the proxy
Sampling rules applied deterministically for test cases (route-based + tenant override)
End-to-end request demonstrates <1ms median added latency at ingress in p50 synthetic traffic
Full trace continuity across proxy -> service A -> service B verified in staging for both instrumented and uninstrumented clients
Metrics emitted to prometheus-compatible endpoint (ingress_latency_ms, sampling_rate_pct, async_queue_depth, dropped_spans_total)
Dashboard tile created in Console showing ingress latency, sampling rate, and queue health; alert rules for queue depth and dropped spans
SDK middleware adapters for Go and Node exist and pass integration tests (happy path + sampled/not-sampled)
tasks: Design and review API surface for proxy annotations and sdk shim (PRD + open design doc)
Implement propagation normalizers (W3C, B3, legacy) in proxy
Implement central sampling engine with override table and rate-limited fallbacks
Integrate async queue + background spanizer; instrument metrics and failures
Add Go and Node middleware bindings that use the proxy's annotation API
End-to-end integration tests and load bench for ingress latency
Create Console dashboard and alerting rules for new metrics
Run security review and threat model for handling tenant tokens and headers
Rollout to canary cluster, compare traces and metrics, run rollback plan
comments: 2026-02-16 - Maya Chen: Initial PRD uploaded and shared with infra and SDK leads. Asked for feedback on sampling rule schema.

2026-02-20 - Diego Rivera: Spike completed — prototype normalizer that accepts traceparent and B3 and rewrites to canonical W3C format. Observed ~0.6ms median overhead on a 1000rps bench (1 worker, no batching).
2026-02-23 - SRE (internal): Concern about queue growth during traffic spikes. Suggested backpressure + circuit-breaker and alerting thresholds. Added to tasks.
2026-02-26 - Security (internal): Confirmed requirement for explicit token redaction in logs. Security review required before deploy to production.
2026-02-28 - Design review: Agreed to keep the SDK shim minimal — only start/end annotations and an optional attributes map. Heavy attribute enrichment belongs in async worker.
2026-03-01 - Diego Rivera: Implemented async spanizer prototype and exposed prometheus metrics; pushed draft PR for review (see links). Next: integrate sampling engine and create integration tests.
